The answer is **C**. The son was an intended beneficiary, but his rights had not vested when the owner and landscaper changed the payee: he learned of the contract only after the owner had paid his father, and he had not relied on it or assented to it. Until rights vest, the contracting parties can modify or discharge the beneficiary's rights, so the son cannot enforce the original term. The shared note says the answer is A or B, but I'm keeping C because those options ignore the vesting rule, which turns on the timing of the modification.

CONFIDENCE: 65
